heading: Free time = gaps in merged busy intervals
body: To find when **all** employees are free, flatten all schedules into one list, sort by start time, merge overlapping intervals, then **look for gaps** between consecutive merged intervals. Those gaps are the common free time.

heading: Why merge first?
body: If Employee A is busy `[2,4]` and Employee B is busy `[3,5]`, the team is busy `[2,5]` — not two separate blocks. Merging overlapping intervals gives you the **true occupied time**, making gaps easy to spot.

label: Core trick · Python
code:
# 1. Flatten & sort
intervals = sorted([interval for emp in schedule for interval in emp])

# 2. Merge overlaps
merged = []
for iv in intervals:
    if not merged or merged[-1][1] < iv[0]:
        merged.append(iv)
    else:
        merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], iv[1])

# 3. Gaps = free time
free = [[merged[i-1][1], merged[i][0]] for i in range(1, len(merged))]

q: What is the time complexity of this solution?
explain: Sorting the flattened intervals dominates at O(n log n); merge and gap-finding are O(n).
